title: Performance record
description: The canonical record for ONE measured kernel on ONE target: its terms (each with provenance and a validity domain), the diagnostics that may never source a term, and -- required from the first record ever written -- the digest triple that says which hardware revision, which built artifact and which exact bytes the numbers came from. A commit sha alone is not provenance: pins whose checkouts carry declared local edits report permanent drift by design, so the bytes actually read must be digested separately (merlin.common.provenance.source_digest). Terms are validated against performance_term.schema.json in a second pass by merlin.perf.record (the contract loader resolves no cross-document $ref).

kernel.description: The measured workload's name, as the measurement source itself spells it.

target.description: The hardware target, threaded in as a parameter from the descriptor/manifest -- never a literal in library code.

digest.description: The provenance triple. All three parts are REQUIRED and none may be the UNKNOWN token: a record that cannot say what it was measured against is uncitable, and every artifact produced before this field existed is uncitable retroactively.

sources.description: sha256 over the exact bytes the derivation READ (merlin.common.provenance.source_digest). Differs from the commit whenever the tree is dirty, which is precisely when a commit looks right and the numbers are not.

artifacts.description: Built artifact name -> its verified content sha256. A built thing (a compiled model, a packaged suite) has no commit of its own; its identity is its bytes.

pins.description: Pin name -> the full 40-character commit that pin declares, as verified against the live checkout at record time.

notes.description: Verification remarks that are real but not drift -- chiefly declared local edits whose digests matched. Carried so a result citing 'that commit PLUS those bytes' says so.

sources.description: Every input this record drew on, each declared citable or diagnostic. The role is what makes 'diagnostics can never source a term' checkable rather than a convention: a term whose provenance.evidence names a diagnostic source is rejected.

role.description: citable = may back a term. diagnostic = recorded for comparison only, never a term's evidence.

digest.description: Content digest of this source, or "UNKNOWN".

terms.description: name -> performance term. Each value is validated against performance_term.schema.json.

diagnostics.description: Numbers recorded for comparison that may NEVER source a term. A peer cycle model that disagrees with the hardware truth by up to ~3x is useful as a cross-check and disqualifying as evidence; keeping it here rather than dropping it preserves the disagreement instead of hiding it.

source.description: Must name a source declared with role 'diagnostic'.

workload.description: What was run, as the measurement source describes it (shapes, op counts, footprint). Inputs, not results.
